new_entities.name: Radioactive iodine for Graves disease
new_entities.description: Use of radioactive iodine as definitive therapy for Graves hyperthyroidism.

new_entities.name: Graves orbitopathy
new_entities.description: Development or worsening of thyroid-associated orbitopathy, including inflammatory or progressive eye manifestations in Graves disease.

edges.effect_quant: Randomized evidence and systematic review support a real eye-disease penalty from radioactive iodine compared with antithyroid drug therapy. A systematic review of 10 RCTs found increased Graves orbitopathy risk with RAI versus antithyroid drugs (RR 4.23), and the landmark Bartalena trial found development or worsening of orbitopathy in 15% after RAI versus 3% with methimazole.
edges.population: patients with Graves hyperthyroidism treated with radioactive iodine, especially those with mild pre-existing eye disease or other orbitopathy risk factors
edges.mechanism: Radioactive iodine may transiently intensify thyroid autoimmunity and worsen post-treatment hypothyroidism-driven immune signaling, increasing the likelihood of new or worsening thyroid eye disease.
edges.summary: This is a harmful edge and one of the best-established treatment tradeoffs in Graves disease. The magnitude is not huge in absolute terms for every patient, but it is clinically important enough that steroid prophylaxis is standard in higher-risk patients.
edges.caveats: The excess risk is clearest when RAI is compared with antithyroid drugs rather than surgery. Prompt correction of hypothyroidism and selective glucocorticoid prophylaxis reduce but do not erase the concern.

evidence.citation: Acharya SH et al 2008 Clin Endocrinol (Oxf)
evidence.notes: Radioiodine therapy (RAI) for Graves' disease (GD) and the effect on ophthalmopathy: a systematic review.

effect_quant.comparator: development or worsening of Graves ophthalmopathy with RAI versus antithyroid drugs

evidence.citation: Bartalena L et al 1998 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Relation between therapy for hyperthyroidism and the course of Graves' ophthalmopathy.

effect_quant.comparator: development or worsening of ophthalmopathy with radioiodine versus methimazole (15% vs 3%)
